---
title: "Modeling Categorical Linear Regression"
---

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
set.seed(222)

set_theme(theme_bw())
```


```{r}
# All soil core data
soil_cores <- read_csv('recorded_lectures/exide-soil-cores.csv') |> 
    filter(pb_ppm <= 5000)

# Sample from the expanded areas
ena_esa <- soil_cores |> 
    # create an "area" column
    mutate(area = str_sub(property_id, 1, 3)) |> 
    # keep only the rows in the expanded data
    filter(area %in% c("ENA", "ESA")) |> 
    # slice a smaller sample
    slice_sample(n = 40, by = area)
```

First, let's visualize the data. With a categorical predictor, _jitter_ the x-axis so the points dont overlap.

```{r}
ggplot(ena_esa, aes(area, pb_ppm)) +
    geom_point(
        shape = 21,
        fill = "cornflowerblue",
        color = "white",
        alpha = 0.5,
        # jitter the points left to right for easier visualization
        position = position_jitter(width = 0.15, height = 0, seed = 222)
    )
```

Now, fit the model with `lm()`

```{r}
# The formula is te same whether the predictor is continuous or categorical
ena_esa_lm <- lm(pb_ppm ~ area, data = ena_esa)
         # response ^     # ^ predictor
```

Use `summary()` to see the coefficients and other properties of the model.

```{r}
summary(ena_esa_lm)
```
